subject: ela

sections.scope_note: Arizona standards deferred per Ivan (2026-10-03). This crosswalk covers Florida B.E.S.T. ELA ↔ IB PYP Language only.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies character traits, feelings, and motivations. PYP frames this through inquiry into perspective and meaning-making.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use character perspective journals where students track a character's changing motivations through a story, connecting to PYP inquiry questions about perspective.

rows.key_differences: Florida requires explaining how theme develops using details. PYP emphasizes making connections across texts and to broader concepts.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Create theme-tracking anchor charts that connect story details to larger life themes, supporting both explicit theme identification and PYP conceptual connections.

rows.topic_domain: Reading Literary Text - Perspective and Point of View
rows.key_differences: Florida distinguishes perspective from narrative point of view. PYP integrates perspective as a key concept across all learning.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use perspective-taking activities where students rewrite scenes from different characters' viewpoints, developing both analytical and empathetic skills.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Transdisciplinary Theme: How we express ourselves
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies four poem types (free verse, rhymed verse, haiku, limerick). PYP focuses on poetry as expression without mandating specific forms.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Integrate poetry form study with 'How we express ourselves' unit, having students both identify forms and create their own poems as expressions of inquiry.

rows.topic_domain: Reading Informational Text - Text Features and Structure
rows.key_differences: Florida lists specific structures (chronology, comparison, cause/effect). PYP emphasizes understanding how texts are organized to convey meaning.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: During unit research, explicitly teach text structure identification as a research skill, connecting to PYP inquiry into how information is organized.

rows.topic_domain: Reading Informational Text - Central Idea and Details
rows.key_differences: Both emphasize identifying main ideas and supporting details. PYP frames this as a thinking skill applied across transdisciplinary learning.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use graphic organizers for central idea/details across all subject inquiries, building transferable comprehension skills.

rows.topic_domain: Reading Informational Text - Author's Evidence and Claims
rows.key_differences: Florida separates evidence identification from claim-evidence relationship. PYP develops critical thinking as an integrated skill.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Build critical reading routines: 'What is the author claiming? What evidence supports it? Is it convincing?' aligned with PYP inquiry questioning.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Transdisciplinary Theme: How we express ourselves
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies metaphor, personification, hyperbole. PYP addresses figurative language within broader language development without listing specific types.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Create a class figurative language museum with examples from inquiry texts, connecting literary analysis to 'How we express ourselves' theme.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies different summary elements for literary (plot+theme) vs. informational (central idea+details). PYP treats summarizing as a communication skill.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Practice summarizing inquiry findings using genre-appropriate structures, building both comprehension and communication skills.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Transdisciplinary Theme: How we express ourselves
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies sequence, description, dialogue, transitions, ending. PYP emphasizes writing for authentic purposes and audiences.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Connect narrative writing to inquiry topics—students write stories that explore unit concepts, meeting both technical requirements and authentic purpose.

rows.key_differences: Florida requires text-based evidence and transitions. PYP emphasizes reasoned arguments and principled communication.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use debate and discussion protocols where students form opinions based on inquiry evidence, developing both writing and oral argumentation skills.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies introduction, facts, elaboration, transitions, conclusion. PYP frames expository writing as sharing inquiry learning.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use unit exhibition writing as authentic expository writing practice, applying Florida structural requirements to share inquiry findings.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies sequence, nonverbal cues, volume, pronunciation. PYP develops oral communication across all learning contexts.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Integrate formal presentation skills into inquiry sharing, using rubrics that address both Florida requirements and PYP communication skills.

rows.key_differences: Florida lists specific conventions to master (verb tenses, plurals, quotation marks, etc.). PYP develops conventions through authentic writing.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Teach conventions explicitly but apply them in meaningful contexts—editing inquiry writing for publication, peer feedback on convention use.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies academic vocabulary, Greek/Latin roots, and context clues. PYP develops vocabulary across transdisciplinary learning.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Create unit vocabulary walls with academic terms, roots/affixes, and context strategies, building transferable word-learning skills across subjects.
